title: Senior Backend Engineer, AI Engineering: Chat
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Duo Chat team, focused on Chat Engine, you'll build the core AI capabilities behind GitLab Duo Chat, the natural-language and agentic interface to the GitLab DevSecOps platform. Much of your work will involve building flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry, the Python framework built on LangGraph within our Duo Workflow Service that powers agentic chat, and integrating them with the GitLab Rails monolith.</p> <p>You'll own complex backend features from start to finish across both services. You'll integrate large language models and orchestrate multi-agent flows so customers can work faster and more securely across the software development lifecycle. This work sits where GitLab's core platform meets its AI strategy, and reliability, performance, and answer quality directly shape the customer experience.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Design and build flow components and agentic flows in the Flow Registry using Python and LangGraph within the Duo Workflow Service. These reusable building blocks power agentic Duo Chat and, increasingly, other AI features across GitLab.</li> <li>Develop, ship, and maintain backend features for GitLab Duo Chat across the Python Duo Workflow Service and the GitLab Rails monolith in a secure, well-tested, and performant way.</li> <li>Integrate new generative AI models, providers, tools, and multi-agent orchestration patterns into Duo Chat to expand its capabilities and improve answer quality.</li> <li>Design, implement, and review GraphQL and Representational State Transfer (REST) application programming interfaces (APIs) and related monolith logic, including chat entry points, permissions, and foundational-flow registration. Keep contracts with frontend clients and host systems reliable and clear.</li> <li>Improve debugging, observability, and test coverage using pytest, RSpec, and related frameworks; track and improve latency, error rates, and test coverage so AI-powered chat workflows stay reliable at scale.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, User Experience (UX), frontend, and AI specialists to refine requirements and deliver high-quality improvements through iteration.</li> <li>Document standards, patterns, and learnings with other engineers, raising the bar for safe AI integration and evidence-driven engineering.</li> <li>Participate in Tier 2 on-call rotations to troubleshoot production issues, contribute to root cause analysis, and strengthen resiliency.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and maintaining production Python backends, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous or long-running workloads.</li> <li>Practical experience designing and shipping AI-powered, agentic backend features, including large language model integration, tool or function calling, and multi-agent orchestration. You use sound judgment about large language model limitations and safe use in production.</li> <li>Working proficiency in Ruby on Rails, or a strong willingness to learn it. Duo Chat integrates deeply with the GitLab monolith for chat entry points, GraphQL, permissions, and flow registration, and most of GitLab's codebase is written in Ruby.</li> <li>Proficiency designing or extending REST or GraphQL APIs with attention to scalability, maintainability, and backward compatibility.</li> <li>Strong Structured Query Language (SQL) skills and familiarity with relational databases such as PostgreSQL, including efficient queries and data modeling.</li> <li>Ability to find, diagnose, and prevent performance and reliability problems at scale.</li> <li>Experience solving technical problems of high scope and complexity and advocating for quality, security, and performance improvements across your team.</li> <li>Openness to learning and collaborating in an async-first, distributed team, applying transferable skills from related technologies or domains. Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph or LangChain is a strong plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're part of GitLab's AI Engineering organization and own the AI-powered chat experience embedded across the GitLab platform. Chat Engine is the backend-focused team within the Duo Chat group.</p> <p>We're backend, frontend, and AI specialists working asynchronously across time zones, using issues, merge requests, and documentation as our main collaboration tools. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Architecture Engineering: Nonlinear Productivity
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team, you'll find and remove friction across the software development lifecycle using reliable AI-powered automation — diagnosing problems like long review cycles, manual release steps, and brittle automation, then building the automation and process changes that resolve them for good.</p> <p>Some examples of the problems this team takes on:</p> <ul> <li>Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.</li> <li>Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Identify sources of friction across GitLab's software development lifecycle and scope agentic solutions to address them, turning vague pain points into concrete, buildable proposals.</li> <li>Design and build reliable AI-powered systems that follow step-by-step workflows, use tools and safety checks, and correct errors before taking engineering action — the kind of output you can actually trust with real engineering decisions.</li> <li>Build and maintain evaluation tools that judge agent output on correctness, constraint compliance, and cost, not on whether it merely "seems to work."</li> <li>Work across GitLab's codebase as each problem requires, going wherever the friction actually is rather than staying inside one service or product area.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to identify generated code that may fail under concurrency, at scale, or across self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant deployments, catching failures before they reach customers.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group, sharing roadmaps, findings, and reusable agent tooling</li> <li>Take ownership of a greenfield problem space from day one, helping shape a proven internal fix into a capability GitLab could offer customers externally, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Hands-on experience building agentic or large language model-based systems — multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery patterns — and making them reliable in production, not treated as one-off prompts or demonstrations.</li> <li>A track record of working autonomously in unfamiliar codebases, getting oriented quickly, and driving solutions through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems knowledge, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, in that order of team priority, and the ability to read and modify code in the other languages.</li> <li>Helpful experience includes shipping autonomous agents that complete real tasks from start to finish; improving build systems, release processes, review workflows, or other parts of the software development lifecycle; and working with globally distributed teams, large language model workload costs, or production constraints across on-premises, air-gapped, single-tenant, and software-as-a-service deployments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. It operates like a startup — no dedicated product manager, no pre-set backlog — and solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.</p> <p>It's a good fit for engineers who'd rather go find the next problem than be handed one, and who want a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.</p> <p> </p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. A primary focus for this role is building proactive data growth controls for GitLab.com, including retention and lifecycle management frameworks, enforcement of retention policies at schema-change time, and tooling that keeps database growth sustainable as AI-driven development accelerates how quickly data accumulates. You'll help teams across GitLab reason confidently about data architecture, placement, and lifecycle management, while proactively identifying saturation points in our GitLab.com infrastructure and driving corrective actions with partner teams. With the team's recent move into the Data Engineering organization, you'll also shape new scalability and data health features for self-managed customers, working hands-on with PostgreSQL and Ruby on Rails in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/22105">Data Growth Controls (retention enforcement and data lifecycle management)</a></li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/17719"><u><span class="textUnderline">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</span></u></a></li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/epics/16152"><u><span class="textUnderline">Background Operations Framework</span></u></a></li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Develop and iterate backend features and data frameworks that make it safe and efficient for GitLab teams to work with data at scale across SaaS and self-managed deployments.</li> <li value="2">Design and build data retention and lifecycle management frameworks, including retention policy enforcement, bulk data removal tooling, and automated identification of tables that need retention policies.</li> <li value="3">Build shift-left guardrails, such as static analysis checks and schema-change-time enforcement, that catch unsustainable data growth patterns before they reach production.</li> <li value="4">Collaborate closely with product management, UX, frontend, infrastructure, software delivery, and analytics teams to design and ship high-performing solutions</li> <li value="5">Review and improve database-related changes from other engineers and community contributors, ensuring data integrity, safety, and performance across all deployment scenarios.</li> <li value="6">Design, build, and maintain tooling such as SQL traffic replay and background operations frameworks to proactively surface and address scalability and performance issues.</li> <li value="7">Research, design, and implement improvements to data retention and lifecycle management, database performance, scalability, and data health, including areas like soft delete strategies and database migration testing.</li> <li value="8">Document database best practices, patterns to avoid, and data architecture guidance to enable developers to make informed decisions.</li> <li value="9">Develop proactive tooling and guardrails that help developers detect and remediate potential performance and data issues early in the development lifecycle.</li> <li value="10"> </li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including high availability solutions with automatic failover and zero-downtime data migrations as well as managing large or fast-growing datasets through approaches such as data retention, archiving, partitioning, or lifecycle management.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Ruby on Rails or another Ruby framework, including designing, implementing, and reviewing backend features.</li> <li value="3">Ability to reason about software design, algorithms, and performance trade-offs at a system level.</li> <li value="4">Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.</li> <li value="5">Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills and the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one".</li> <li value="6">Alignment with GitLab's values, including transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and contribution to open source.</li> <li value="7">Openness to learning and applying new tools and approaches, including transferable experience from related data, infrastructure, or developer tooling domains.</li> <li value="8">Willingness to participate in our <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/#tier-2-on-call">tier 2 dabase on-call rotation</a> in your time zone.</li> </ul> <p>The <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence Group</a> is a remote, agile backend team that builds and maintains the frameworks, patterns, and tooling that enable GitLab teams to work confidently with data at scale across all application datastores. title: Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team sits within GitLab's Developer Experience group and builds the platforms our engineers rely on every day. GitLab engineers increasingly build software with artificial intelligence agents. Agents can generate code and tests in seconds, but they can also produce passing test suites for software that doesn't work as intended. As a Senior Backend Engineer, Trusted Agentic Development, you'll own the technical thesis for closing that validation gap and build the early proof yourself. You'll rethink what validation means when the author is an agent and make the feedback loop fast, automatic, and trustworthy enough that teams choose to adopt it.</p> <ul> <li value="1">Validation that confirms agent-generated code does what was intended, so a passing suite means a working feature and not just a satisfied proxy.</li> <li value="2">Mid-loop feedback that helps an agent self-correct toward working software instead of green assertions.</li> <li value="3">Language-aware approaches under one shared model of what "trusted" means, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, while allowing the right technique to differ by language.</li> <li value="4">Real measurement of whether engineers trust and adopt the path, fed straight back into the platform.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the technical thesis for how GitLab validates software when an agent is the author, and turn it into an architecture the team can build against.</li> <li value="2">Prototype the hard parts by building early versions of feedback mechanisms that catch the gap between passing tests and working software, proving what works before the team scales it.</li> <li value="3">Develop approaches for GitLab's primary stacks, starting with Rust, Ruby, and Go, under one shared definition of "trusted," while allowing the right technique to differ by language.</li> <li value="4">Design the mid-loop feedback an agent needs to self-correct toward working software rather than green assertions, and build the systems that deliver it.</li> <li value="5">Collaborate with engineering teams to adopt these approaches, measure adoption, engineer trust, and validation quality, and use those findings to improve the platform.</li> <li value="6">Set technical direction the team can build on, review designs, and help teammates grow their technical judgment.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Deep, current, hands-on experience building real software with artificial intelligence agents, ideally across more than one language, and a clear understanding of why agent output can pass tests yet fail in production.</li> <li value="2">A strong point of view on the validation gap and concrete ideas for closing it, backed by approaches you've built or tried.</li> <li value="3">Experience designing distributed systems designed to run on Kubernetes first.</li> <li value="3">The technical range to design systems rather than tune a single framework, and the judgment to know when a solution should be general or language-specific.</li> <li value="4">You prototype to learn, and you ship.</li> <li value="5">The ability to influence engineers across an organization without formal authority through working code and sound reasoning.</li> <li value="6">Strong written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li value="7">Alignment with GitLab's values, especially collaboration, iteration, and transparency.</li> </ul> <p>This isn't a quality assurance or test automation role. We aren't looking for depth in a particular testing framework. We're looking for someone who has built with agents, experienced the validation gap firsthand, and wants to solve it.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Trusted Agentic Development team is part of GitLab's Developer Experience group. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Customer Success Architect, you'll serve as a trusted strategic advisor and technical authority to some of GitLab's most complex and high-value Enterprise and Government customers across Singapore. In this role, you will be driving and shaping how our largest customers adopt GitLab's intelligent DevSecOps platform to achieve their business goals and realise meaningful, long-term outcomes. You will be working closely with customers after the sale to turn pre-sales command plans into clear success plans, guide them through their customer journey, and drive adoption, utilization, and technical maturity. You will also be directly influencing renewal and expansion decisions through your post-sales engagements with executive-level decision makers in the account.</p> <p>This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who has already led high-stakes pre or post sales customer engagements in large complex accounts across multiple industry domains to drive quantifiable business outcomes..The individual is comfortable operating with  ambiguity, and can credibly advise VP- and C-level stakeholders on business transformation, application modernization, platform strategy, architecture, and organizational DevSecOps transformation. You'll also be shaping playbooks and best practices, and acting as an escalation point for the team's most technically or politically complex situations.</p> <p>Reporting into the APJ Customer Success organization, you'll own a portfolio of GitLab's most strategic enterprise and Government accounts, act as the executive-level technical liaison for these accounts, and drive cross-functional resolution of their highest-priority issues — coordinating and, where needed, directing the efforts of Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Professional Services, and Support. You'll bring deep technical expertise in CI/CD, cloud platforms, multi-cloud, hybrid architecture and enterprise DevSecOps practices.You will use that expertise to shape customers' long-term platform strategy, apply best practices, configure GitLab for their environments and stay current with platform capabilities. In your first year, success will look like establishing yourself as the trusted senior advisor across a portfolio of flagship accounts, building strong relationships with key stakeholders, materially improving and increasing platform maturity, leading retention and renewal conversations, increasing customer satisfaction across your portfolio and contributing to the broader CSA team's technical standards and ways of working.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>Turning pre-sales command plans into measurable customer success plans that align technical adoption with business outcomes</li> <li>Leading and driving the technical strategy behind a large-scale DevSecOps platform consolidation for a regulated Enterprise account or Government, including guiding enterprise customers on GitLab best practices across CI/CD, DevSecOps, cloud architecture, TCO, applying compliance and architecture as well as business case presentations to customer executives</li> <li>Owning end-to-end resolution of a critical, multi-team escalation for a flagship account — driving root cause analysis, coordinating Engineering/Product/Support, and personally briefing customer executives on remediation</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Owns a book of Enterprise and Government customers and drive adoption, retention, expansion, and overall satisfaction through ongoing strategic, business and technical engagement.</li> <li>Serves as the senior post-sales strategic, business and technical advisor for a portfolio of GitLab's most complex, highest-value enterprise and Government accounts, shaping multi-year platform and DevSecOps strategy in partnership with customer executives, coordinating responses to questions, issues, and escalations across Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services. <em> </em></li> <li>Translates ambiguous, high-stakes business outcomes into rigorous Customer Success Plans that are regularly reviewed with customer stakeholders. The Customer Success Plans contain clearly defined business outcome related goals, quantifiable benefits, realistic adoption milestones and remediation actions. </li> <li>Prepares executive-ready reporting conducted on a regular basis with clear accountability for outcomes that demonstrate impact on adoption, retention, and expansion of GitLab products and services.</li> <li>Provides deep technical guidance on enterprise-scale CI/CD architecture, DevSecOps maturity models, platform consolidation strategy, including advising on complex trade-offs (e.g., multi-cloud vs. hybrid, self-managed vs. GitLab Dedicated, etc).</li> <li>Owns the full lifecycle of your account portfolio's adoption, retention, and expansion outcomes, with direct accountability for the commercial and technical health of flagship relationships.</li> <li>Leads end-to-end resolution of critical, cross-functional account escalations, ensuring root causes are identified, follow-up actions are owned, holding internal teams accountable to timelines, driving the root cause analysis and personally managing executive communication and risk.<em> </em></li> <li>Leads end-to-end resolution of critical, cross-functional account escalations, ensuring   root causes are identified, follow-up actions are owned, holding internal teams accountable to timelines, driving the driving root cause analysis and personally managing executive communication and risk.</li> <li>Designs and delivers technical enablement programs at scale, identifying systemic maturity gaps across a portfolio and building the roadmap (not just individual sessions) that closes them.</li> <li>Advises key customers stakeholders on cloud and platform architecture decisions with enterprise-wide impact, which includes  multi-region deployment strategy, secrets management architecture and network/security topology for regulated environments.</li> <li>Guides customers on GitLab platform best practices including Git workflows, branching strategies, CI/CD pipeline design, DevSecOps adoption patterns, and security scanning configuration. </li> <li>Provides hands-on technical enablement and onboarding, including education on GitLab features, releases, and use cases, and identification of training and maturity opportunities aligned to customer goals. </li> <li>Engages customers on cloud platform architecture decisions relevant to their GitLab deployment — including self-managed vs. GitLab Dedicated, Runner configuration and auto-scaling, secrets management, and network topology considerations. </li> <li>Advises customers on DevSecOps consolidation value — articulating the TCO, compliance, and developer experience case for platform consolidation over fragmented toolchains. </li> <li>Collaborates with Professional Services, Sales, and internal teams to identify expansion opportunities, recommend enablement interventions, and ensure a seamless customer journey from onboarding through renewal. </li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Must be a Singapore Citizen and based in Singapore</li> <li>Mandatory English language proficiency</li> <li>Hands-on experience building or owning CI/CD pipelines end to end, including pipeline as code, multi-stage design, artifact management, and troubleshooting in real-world environments.</li> <li>A career built across different direct customer facing engagement roles such as Technical Account Management, Technical Solution Sales, Pre-sales, Business Development, Consulting, Professional services across customers in different industry vertical domains like Government, Banking, Financial and Insurance Services, Manufacturing, Telecommunications, engagement with multiple technology and platform paths.</li> <li>Create and improve upon the processes, metrics and KPIs for SME-led technical evaluations, workshops, demos and Proofs of Value.</li> <li>Partner with CRO staff, regional sales leaders and AVPs on product-category performance, forecast risk and competitive strategy.</li> <li>Partner with Enablement to drive  field readiness for new product launches with Product Marketing and Enablement, including Duo Agent Platform, security and platform offerings.</li> <li>Build strong relationships with key customers at the technical sponsor and executive level.</li> <li>Use AI to change how the team works, including deal research, demo creation, PoV automation and knowledge sharing.</li> <li>Drive organizational transformation by finding gaps early, building structure where none exists, and leading change without waiting for top-down direction.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>5+ years second-line leadership experience (managing managers) security or developer tools.</li> <li>A record of tying technical-team design to bookings and consumption outcomes, with the data to show it.</li> <li>The ability to lead through ambiguity and rapid title: Senior Partner Solutions Manager, Strategic Partnerships
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As a Senior Partner Solutions Manager, Strategic Partnerships, you'll own the technical strategy and validation of joint work with GitLab's strategic partners: hyperscalers, artificial intelligence (AI) labs, AI-native companies, and development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) vendors. You'll work with partners, Product, and Research and Development (R&D) to turn partner and customer needs into integrations, influence product design, and build the business case for each joint effort, from the first architecture review to a shipped integration. In this role you will also own the AI model evaluation process with our model partners, working closely with our R&D teams to assess new models ahead of release and ensure GitLab is built on the best-performing models for our customers. Unlike a customer-facing Solutions Architect role focused on adoption, you'll work with partners to make GitLab better. This role has no sales quota or variable pay.</p> <p>At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Our platform doesn't just bring people together-it unites teams and organizations, breaking down barriers and redefining what's possible in software development.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Own the end-to-end technical strategy for assigned strategic partners, connecting technical requirements with joint business objectives.</li> <li>Turn partner technology and roadmaps into integration, architecture, and product opportunities across the GitLab platform, from planning to monitoring and AI agents and model integrations.</li> <li>Resolve complex technical issues across GitLab and partner systems, including cloud architecture, tool integrations, and AI model and agent evaluation and integration. Build working prototypes to validate concepts with partners.</li> <li>Manage the end-to-end AI model evaluation process with our model partners, coordinating with R&D to secure early access, align on evaluation criteria and timelines, and translate results into partnership and product roadmap decisions.</li> <li>Design and facilitate partner workshops, architecture reviews, and cloud financial management (FinOps) sessions, bringing in the right participants and documenting outcomes and next steps.</li> <li>Build business cases for joint technical efforts, defining expected gains, costs, and resources, and securing agreement from partner managers, R&D, and leadership.</li> <li>Bring partner requirements and technical feedback into Product and R&D discussions to influence product design and the roadmap.</li> <li>Coordinate Engineering, Product, FinOps, Finance, Sales, and Marketing with partner technical teams to move joint work from evaluation to delivery.</li> <li>Track cloud, AI, and DevSecOps developments to advise partnership investment, and share reusable findings through documentation, the handbook, reference architectures, and technical content.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience as a Senior Solutions Architect, Partner Solutions Architect, Partner Engineer, or in a similar senior technical role. Experience with technology partners or alliances is strongly preferred.</li> <li>An end-to-end understanding of the software development lifecycle, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and DevSecOps, with the ability to use GitLab in depth.</li> <li>Hands-on cloud architecture experience with at least one hyperscaler: Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Microsoft Azure. Engineering leaders and their teams.</li> <li>Use data and qualitative feedback to identify trends in the Engineering organization and recommend actions that improve effectiveness, engagement, and performance.</li> <li>Support the planning and execution of Engineering offsites and other key forums so leaders can align on priorities, make decisions, and move work forward efficiently.</li> Directors and VPs, building trusted relationships, influencing decisions, and providing clear, data-informed guidance.</li> <li>Experience supporting globally distributed teams, including working across multiple regions and time zones and navigating regional differences such as those in EMEA.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to help organizations navigate through change or transformation, such as job architecture updates, leadership transitions, or shifts in team structure and culture, while balancing strategic work such as organizational design, leadership effectiveness, and culture initiatives with hands-on execution of core People processes.</li> <li>Strong coaching, communication and collaboration skills, including working asynchronously and partnering cross-functionally with Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards, and other People teams.</li> <li>Openness to learning GitLab's ways of working and applying transferable experience from related domains, such as Product or IT, development lifecycle knowledge, is comfortable working with technical teams, and wants to help create something new in DevSecOps.</p> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Define and drive product strategy for experiences that connect planning, source code management, and AI-assisted development.</li> <li>Shape workflows where teams and agents move between intent and code in both directions, so a specification can be traced to the merges that implement it and a diff can be read and reviewed against the intent behind it.</li> <li>Work with engineering, design, and other product teams to build product experiences that support human-in-the-loop and autonomous development workflows.</li> <li>Partner with teams working on demos and prototypes, including near-term work around spec-driven planning and autonomous development modes, including which decisions stay with a human and why.</li> <li>Use customer insights, product usage data, and market context to identify opportunities that can deliver customer value quickly.</li> <li>Help teams ship fast with quality, balancing near-term execution with longer-term product direction.</li> <li>Explore how planning can better account for reviewing code, reviewing test cases, and validating that work produced by agents matches the intended outcome.</li> <li>Collaborate across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI product areas to reduce friction across the software development lifecycle.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What You’ll Bring</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li>Experience as a product manager working on developer tools, DevOps tools, source code management, planning tools, AI-native products, or related software development lifecycle products.</li> <li>Direct, hands-on experience with the source code lifecycle, including branches, merge requests, code review, CI/CD, and releases, whether as a product manager or as an engineer, along with a strong understanding of how software moves from ideas and requirements through planning, coding, review, testing, and delivery.</li> <li>Experience working with technical product areas and engineering teams, with enough technical depth to understand developer workflows and tradeoffs.</li> <li>A data-forward approach to product management, including experience using data to identify customer impact and guide prioritization.</li> <li>Comfort operating in ambiguous spaces where there may not yet be a clear market pattern or established product category.</li> <li>Experience building or shipping with AI tools and agents, not just using them, and a point of view of your own on where AI helps and where it does not across the software development lifecycle.</li> <li>Ability to think creatively about how AI changes the software development lifecycle and how product experiences should adapt.</li> <li>Strong collaboration and communication skills, especially in an all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>A bias toward action and the ability to help teams ship meaningful customer value quickly.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>About the team</strong></span></h2> <p>This role sits within the Product organization and will work closely with teams across Plan, Source Code Management, Code Review, and AI. You'll own the backend usage billing pipeline and its product direction while supporting the Monetization Platform and Infrastructure team as it modernizes the foundations underneath it.</p> <p>When another GitLab team launches a credit-consuming capability, you'll help them make it billable across GitLab.com, self-managed, and GitLab Dedicated. This is a technical, systems-oriented product role: success means building a monetization platform other teams can launch on quickly and correctly, rather than shipping customer-facing UI.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the product direction for metering, aggregation, and rating in GitLab's usage billing pipeline, including the Zuora and CustomersDot integrations that turn usage into invoiced revenue.</li> <li>Make onboarding a new credit-consuming capability a repeatable process rather than a bespoke project each time.</li> <li>Partner with product teams on what to instrument, how to meter and price usage across GitLab.com, self-managed, and GitLab Dedicated, and what it takes to be billable on launch day. Stay ahead of their roadmaps so billing doesn't delay launches.</li> <li>Prioritize pipeline scalability, performance, and reliability as consumption grows, balancing those investments against new capability enablement.</li> <li>Own billing defect detection and remediation so errors surface before they reach a customer's invoice and billing outcomes remain auditable.</li> <li>Support the Monetization Platform and Infrastructure team by framing problems, explaining the value of platform investments, and prioritizing them against operational risk.</li> <li>Define and track measures of billing accuracy, pipeline reliability, cost to serve per capability, and time to monetize so teams can make informed pricing decisions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning the product direction of consumption- or usage-based billing systems.</li> <li>Experience with Zuora or a comparable billing and revenue platform, and an understanding of how product and finance systems interact.</li> <li>Experience with prepaid, commitment, or credit-drawdown pricing models (balances, reservations, overage, expiration) and the edge cases they create in billing and revenue.</li> <li>Experience launching new products or pricing models while coordinating across engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance and go-to-market teams.</li> <li>Ability to bring together teams you don't manage around work their launches depend on.</li> <li>Experience defining problems for platform or backend teams whose users are often other teams.</li> <li>Clear written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment; you'll use issues, epics, and direction pages to lead.</li> <li>Familiarity with developer tooling, financial audit or revenue recognition, or an engineering background can help, but isn't required.</li> <li>You use AI tools as part of how you work: prototyping, analysis, spec writing, and investigation.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>In Monetization, we coordinate across engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance and go-to-market on new products and pricing models. Our remote, asynchronous work uses written issues, and epics to keep decisions visible.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Senior Product Manager, CRM & GTM Systems
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An Overview about the Role</strong></p> <p>We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the Lead-to-Opportunity (L2O) domain within our Salesforce and GTM technology ecosystem. This role sits at the intersection of marketing operations, sales process, and technology owning the roadmap for how leads are captured, scored, routed, and converted into pipeline, and how our broader GTM tech stack supports that motion.</p> <p>This is a foundational hire one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA model into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. You'll be both an individual contributor driving your own domain and a mentor helping BSAs grow into product manager roles. You'll have direct influence over how we shape the team's future operating model.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Do</strong></p> <p><strong>Internal Product Roadmap Ownership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define, own, and maintain the multi-quarter internal product roadmap for the Lead-to-Opportunity domain covering lead capture, enrichment, scoring, routing, conversion, opportunity and the broader GTM technology stack integrated with Salesforce</li> <li>Translate business strategy from Marketing, Sales Development, RevOps, and GTM leadership into sequenced, prioritized system capabilities with clear outcomes and success metrics</li> <li>Define the domain's strategic priorities each quarter and half, balancing net-new capability delivery, stabilization, and technical debt reduction with transparent trade-off frameworks</li> <li>Drive quarterly planning ceremonies, partnering with Engineering Managers and BSAs to align capacity with roadmap commitments</li> <li>Own domain-level documentation: process maps, current-vs-future state lead lifecycle flows, and decision logs that keep stakeholders and the team aligned on scope and ownership</li> </ul> <p><strong>Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements Translation</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary product voice for all L2O and GTM Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Marketing, Marketing Operations, SDR/BDR leadership, Sales, and RevOps</li> <li>Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions translating complex GTM and marketing operations requirements into actionable system specifications</li> <li>Own the decision layer between "what the business needs" and "what engineering builds," resolving ambiguity with structured frameworks and documented decisions</li> <li>Run structured stakeholder alignment sessions to surface trade-offs, build consensus, and drive open decisions to closure rather than letting them linger</li> <li>Represent the domain in cross-team planning and leadership reviews able to explain technical constraints to business stakeholders and business context to engineers</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team Mentorship & Capability Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Act as a product craft mentor and senior thought partner for the BSA team, actively upskilling analysts in product thinking, requirements structuring, acceptance criteria definition, and roadmap communication</li> <li>Model and codify what "good" looks like reusable templates, rituals (backlog grooming, roadmap reviews), and a rubric BSAs can grow against</li> <li>Give BSAs increasing ownership over pieces of the roadmap as they develop, with regular feedback and structured check-ins</li> <li>Partner with leadership to evolve the team's operating model from project-execution-focused to product-thinking-led, raising the bar for how EntApps delivers business value</li> </ul> <p><strong>Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead initiatives end-to-end: discovery, requirements, prioritization, solution design review, UAT, launch, and post-launch measurement</li> <li>Write and maintain clear user stories, acceptance criteria, and lead-flow and data-flow diagrams that engineering and admins can build against without ambiguity</li> <li>Manage a healthy, well-groomed backlog intake requests from Marketing and Sales Development, triage by impact and effort, and defend prioritization decisions to stakeholders</li> <li>Define success metrics per initiative (lead response time, routing accuracy, lead-to-opportunity conversion rate, data quality, SDR/BDR adoption) and report on outcomes, not just delivery</li> <li>Identify and de-risk dependencies across adjacent domains campaign operations, data enrichment vendors, opportunity handoff to sales before they block delivery</li> <li>Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release</li> </ul> <p><strong>Systems Architecture Collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers on Salesforce and MarTech integration design marketing automation platform to Salesforce sync, data enrichment pipelines, lead scoring and routing engines, ensuring choices hold up to governance, scale, and future roadmap needs</li> <li>Bring informed opinions on GTM platform architecture trade-offs based on deep domain knowledge</li> <li>Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce Sales Cloud and connected MarTech tools, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds</li> <li>Maintain domain-level R&R clarity, who owns what across US/India technical managers, BSAs, and adjacent pods and update as team and scope evolve</li> <li>Ability to engage deeply with engineering and architecture teams on API design, data modeling, and integration patterns.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>7+ years in Salesforce product management, business systems analysis, or Marketing/Revenue Operations technology roles, with demonstrated growth into product ownership</li> <li>Strong working knowledge of Lead-to-Opportunity processes; lead capture, scoring, routing, and conversion and how they connect marketing execution to sales pipeline</li> <li>Hands-on familiarity with the GTM technology stack: Salesforce Sales Cloud plus marketing automation platforms (Marketo, HubSpot, or Pardot), lead scoring and routing tools, and data enrichment or intent providers</li> <li>Good Understanding of quoting process </li> <li>Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders</li> <li>Proven experience leading initiatives end-to-end with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities, especially across Marketing and Sales</li> <li>Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs — without needing to write code</li> <li>Experience mentoring or upskilling analysts and BSAs, you enjoy developing people, not just managing tickets</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication; able to represent technical trade-offs to non-technical executives and translate business asks into clear technical requirements</li> <li>Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving structure where none exists</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted development workflows, data governance and compliance for lead data, or prior people-management experience</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the Team</strong></p> <p>You'll be one of the first product managers on a team actively transforming from a reactive BSA function into a proactive, roadmap-driven product organization. The Lead-to-Opportunity domain sits at the top of GitLab's revenue funnel; the quality of data, routing, and conversion here affects every downstream system and every seller. Getting this right is not an IT problem; it's a revenue problem. You'll have direct influence over how we shape the team's future operating model and how the next generation of BSAs grows into product managers.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.</em></p></div><div class="title">Uni

title: Senior Product Manager, Secret Detection and Vulnerability Research
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a <strong>Senior Product Manager</strong>, you will own GitLab's Secret Detection offering and the Vulnerability Research function that produces the detection content across security products. Secret Detection is one of the highest-signal, highest-volume security capabilities on the platform. Leaked credentials are the most common initial access vector in real breaches, and as AI agents write, commit, and configure more of the software, the surface area for exposed secrets grows faster than the number of humans watching it.</p> <p>You will own the full loop: detect a secret with high precision, tell the customer whether it is still live, get it revoked, and prevent the next one from ever landing. In parallel, you will own vulnerability research as a product asset rather than a back-office function. The detection rules, advisory data, and malicious package and reference intelligence your team produces are what make GitLab's security scanners worth paying for, and they need to ship on a cadence with measurable quality.</p> <p>This is an outcome-owning role - you will carry adoption, retention, and revenue targets for your area and be expected to explain how your roadmap moves them.</p> <p><strong>Some examples of our projects:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Push protection and pre-receive blocking that stops a credential before it reaches a repository, without wrecking developer flow</li> <li>Secret validity checking and automated revocation partnerships with major cloud and SaaS token issuers</li> <li>Detection content pipelines that turn threat research into shipped rules, with precision and recall tracked per rule</li> <li>Intelligence-driven detection of malicious packages, dependencies, and references entering the software supply chain</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Own</strong> the business outcomes for Secret Detection and Vulnerability Research, including adoption, expansion, competitive win rate, and revenue contribution. Bring a point of view on packaging and pricing, not just features.</li> <li><strong>Set</strong> the strategy for the full secret lifecycle: prevention, detection, validation, revocation, and reporting across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed.</li> <li><strong>Treat</strong> detection content as a product. Define how rules, advisories, and intelligence feeds are sourced, validated, versioned, and measured, and make quality visible to customers.</li> <li><strong>Hold</strong> the line on detection quality. False positives are a product defect and you will own the metrics that prove precision is improving.</li> <li><strong>Work</strong> at the level of the technology. Read the rule syntax, question the entropy heuristics, understand why a scanner missed something, and challenge engineering with informed alternatives.</li> <li><strong>Use</strong> AI to compress the distance between question and answer. Pull your own data, prototype your own flows, synthesize research and competitive input yourself, and bring conclusions rather than requests for someone else to investigate.</li> <li><strong>Build</strong> the case for where AI belongs in the product: triage, rule generation, remediation guidance, and reducing the human review burden per finding.</li> <li><strong>Partner</strong> with engineering, security research, threat intelligence, Field, and GitLab's own Security team, who are one of your most demanding users.</li> <li><strong>Communicate</strong> in writing, asynchronously, with enough precision that a distributed team can act without a meeting.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Domain depth</strong> in application security, vulnerability management, or security research. You have worked on or adjacent to scanners, detection content, threat intelligence, or SDLC security tooling and you know how these products actually get evaluated in a bake-off.</li> <li><strong>Technical credibility</strong> sufficient to earn the respect of a security engineering team. You do not need to have written the scanner, but you should be able to reason about detection logic, data pipelines, CI integration, and the tradeoffs between coverage and noise.</li> <li><strong>Commercial reasoning.</strong> You start from revenue mechanics, buyer motion, and competitive displacement, then work inward to product decisions. Candidates who reason only from feature lists outward are not a fit.</li> <li><strong>Evidence of using AI as a force multiplier</strong> in your own work: research, analysis, data pulls, prototyping, drafting. Consuming a chat assistant occasionally is not the same as restructuring how you work.</li> <li><strong>Judgment under ambiguity.</strong> You bring structured options and a recommendation instead of escalating an open question.</li> <li><strong>Bias for clarity.</strong> You can take a noisy, technical, politically contested problem and produce one page that everyone can align on.</li> <li><strong>Bonus:</strong> hands-on background as a developer, security engineer, red teamer, or researcher; experience with credential and token ecosystems; experience commercializing a data or intelligence asset.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>This role sits in GitLab's Security product management organization, which owns application security testing, vulnerability management, supply chain security, secrets management, and AI governance. The Security Section is central to GitLab's Ultimate tier and to the shift toward consumption-based product revenue, so the work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to company results. You will work asynchronously with engineering, design, and research counterparts across multiple regions, and with the Field teams who take this to market.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. Switchboard is the control plane for Dedicated: it helps internal teams scale upgrades and maintenance, while giving customers a place to configure their infrastructure, understand the health of their environment, and receive critical updates.</p> <p>You'll own the product vision and roadmap, balancing technical and operational needs with a clear, useful customer experience. Product, and Legal, and escalating stalled or high-severity items. </li> <li>Mature and maintain a risk register and quarterly reporting cadence that gives leadership clear visibility into open risk, remediation progress, and trends.</li> <li>Own and mature AI risk management, including AI impact assessments, AI risk assessments, and risk treatments, to support ISO 42001 certification.</li> <li>Design, develop, and implement key risk indicators and supporting metrics for top risks in the risk register.</li> <li>Identify manual, repetitive steps in risk and TPRM workflows and personally findings.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in security risk management, working with security-centric risk management or compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST RMF, NIST 800-39, ISO 31000). Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF) is a plus.</li> <li>Experience designing and executing qualitative and quantitative risk analyses that translate technical risks into measurable business impact. </li> <li>A track record of driving risk assessments, risk registers, and remediation efforts to closure across IT, Procurement, Internal Audit, Legal, Product, and Engineering, in a heavily regulated or multi-entity environment.</li> <li>Experience interpreting technical control requirements and translating them for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Demonstrated bias toward automation: you've personally built scripts, workflows, or AI-enabled tooling that reduced manual risk or GRC work, not just evaluated tools conceptually. </li> <li>Comfort operating with ambiguity, managing multiple concurrent assessments, and reprioritizing under tight deadlines. </li> <li>Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to translate security risks into business risks.</li> <li>Strong understanding of cloud security, SaaS security models, and DevSecOps practices.</li> <li>Relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC) are preferred but not required. </li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The <strong>Security Assurance </strong>organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk across the company. title: Senior Software Engineer, Security Factory: Code Security
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write and in the open source components they depend on.</p> <p>Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.</p> <p>These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.</li> <li>Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats</li> <li>Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats</li> <li>Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation</li> <li>Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis</li> <li>Mentor Intermediate engineers through code review and pairing, and maintain our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices through review</li> <li>Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't</li> <li>Substantial professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust, with depth in at least one. We use both, plus Ruby on the remediation side and Python for some analyzers, and value willingness to work across them.</li> <li>Familiarity with package managers and dependency management in one or more language ecosystems, such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo. Experience building tooling around them is better still.</li> <li>Demonstrated application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE) and the software supply chain</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous problems and shipping with minimal guidance, with the self-motivation and organizational skills suited to a remote, largely asynchronous environment</li> <li>Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems, and to write design proposals that bring a team to a decision</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Helpful experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data, including measuring false positives and missed findings</li> <li>Experience with performance optimization at scale</li> <li>Hands-on program analysis experience, such as parsing, ASTs, or data-flow analysis</li> <li>Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration</li> <li>Experience with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing and dependency scanning. We help developers find and fix security issues in both the code they write and the open source components they depend on, as early as possible.</p> <p>We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section.
